findings.where: services/enc/piCellSync.ts downloadPiCell (remote check before withPiPullSlot, URL built inside the slot from piCache.baseUrl); same pattern in services/EncImportService.ts syncEncFromPi (piBase taken before the index fetch, piCache.viaRemoteAccess read after it)
findings.defect: The boat-LAN-only rule for licensed cells is checked at the wrong moment. downloadPiCell checks piCache.viaRemoteAccess when it is called, then waits in the 3-slot limiter, and only then builds the URL from piCache.baseUrl. baseUrl switches to the tailnet 100.x address whenever the 30 s health check's 2 s LAN probe fails and the tailnet probe succeeds (PiCacheService.checkHealth sets _useRemote = true). withTimeout(p, false, 60 s) also leaves a timed-out job queued, so it can run minutes later on whatever transport is live then. syncEncFromPi has the mirror race: piBase is captured while on the tailnet, the index fetch takes up to 10 s, a health check flips back to LAN, viaRemoteAccess reads false, and the 20 prewarm pulls go to the tailnet piBase. Today's Pi enforces nothing (C-d's enforcement ships later), so this client check is the only guard.
findings.scenario: At the dock, Auto or PYD runs ensureBoatCells(box, {maxCells: 24}). That queues about 21 protected pulls behind 3 slots, each up to 30 s, alongside the chart's hydration walk. Shane steps into the dinghy, or the Pi is busy and the 2 s LAN status probe times out. The next health tick adopts the tailnet over cellular/Starlink. Every queued job now fetches https://100.x:port/api/enc/installed/OC-…/data over remote access, so licensed cells leave the boat's LAN (Roberto follow-up 4; C-d's rule) and land in the vault. No test covers a transport flip while a pull is queued.
findings.fix: Re-check inside the slot, just before fetchVerifiedFromPi: if the cell is protected and (piCache.viaRemoteAccess or !BOAT_CELLS_ON_PHONE), return false. Better still, build protected-cell URLs from the LAN host (config.host), never from baseUrl, so a tailnet base can't be used. In syncEncFromPi, read the remote flag in the same tick as piBase (or compare piBase's host with the LAN host), use that for boatCharts, and re-check per protected pull in the loop. Add a test: fill the 3 slots, queue a 4th protected pull, flip viaRemoteAccess to true, release the slots, and assert no request reaches the tailnet.

findings.defect: The boat registry gets stuck on 'away (tailnet)' for the rest of the session. When the Pi is reachable and `viaRemoteAccess` is true, the async body returns synchronously at :153, before its first await. Its `finally { registering = null }` therefore runs before `registering ??= …` stores the promise. `registering` then keeps a settled 'away' promise forever, and every later ensureBoatRegistry / whenBoatRegistrySettled / ensureBoatCells call returns 'away' with reason 'tailnet' without asking the Pi again. The onStatusChange retry in wire() goes through the same dead promise. Confirmed with a probe: after the first ask over the tailnet, the second ask on the LAN returned 'away', why 'tailnet', with 0 index fetches.
findings.scenario: Ashore, Shane opens the Route tracer over remote access (registry 'away/tailnet'), then walks aboard with the app still alive, so the phone is now on the boat's Wi-Fi. The tracer keeps grading provisionally, and Save/Follow say "Licensed charts open only on Serene Summer's own Wi-Fi, not over remote access. Check it on the boat's Wi-Fi." Closing and reopening the tracer does not help. The auto-sync, the only path that calls noteBoatRegistered, is deferred for as long as the tracer is open. Auto and PYD fail with the tailnet words and the background check finishes 'unavailable'. It recovers only after the tracer closes and the 10-min poll runs syncEncFromPi over the LAN, or after sign-out or unpair.
findings.fix: Store the promise before the body can settle. For example, `if (!registering) { registering = run(); void registering.finally(() => { registering = null; }); } return registering;` with the clean-up removed from inside run(), or start run() with `await Promise.resolve()`. Add a test: tailnet first → 'away/tailnet'; then viaRemoteAccess false → ensureBoatRegistry() fetches the index and returns 'loaded'.

findings.where: services/EncImportService.ts:668-671 (syncEncFromPi index catch); components/vessel/EncCellManager.tsx:400 (no registry kick); services/enc/piCellSync.ts boatChartsNow
findings.defect: The registry can stay 'pending' indefinitely, and boatChartsNow() keeps returning 'opening' while nothing is opening, so the map notice and the Charts card say "Opening <boat>'s charts from the Pi…". There are two causes. (a) syncEncFromPi throws on an index failure before it reaches noteBoatAway or registerFromPiIndex. That covers a signature or validation failure, a 5xx, and C-d's 401/403 for an unenrolled device. The auto-sync, the only caller when the Pi is reachable, therefore leaves the state at idle→'pending'. Confirmed with a probe: after the failed index, the state was 'pending' and the words were 'opening'. (b) Nothing calls ensureBoatRegistry until MapHub mounts (the auto-sync starts in useEncChartInventory, and the map mounts only on the first visit), the tracer opens, the Log page's background check runs or a route is asked for. The app boots on The Glass and the boot idle re-check is dark. EncCellManager only reads the state.
findings.scenario: (b) Ashore, after a relaunch, The Glass → Vessel → Boat Network → Charts reads "Opening Serene Summer's charts from the Pi…" instead of the away words, and it never changes on that page. Aboard, the same card lists none of her licensed charts and keeps saying 'Opening…' until she visits the map. (a) Aboard with a Pi whose index is refused (for example a crew phone not enrolled once Pi update 3 enforces C-d), the map's no-chart notice says 'Opening…' for the whole session. This fails the lens requirement for honest words while the registry loads and honest words ashore.
findings.fix: (a) In syncEncFromPi's index catch, call noteBoatAway('away'). It is a no-op once loaded, and it also covers the 'pi-needs-update' and 401 cases mapped to the away words. (b) In EncCellManager, add `useEffect(() => { if (boatRegistryState() === 'pending') void ensureBoatRegistry(); }, [])`. Alternatively, make boatChartsNow return 'opening' only while a registration is actually in flight (registering !== null) and otherwise kick it. Add a test for each.

findings.defect: Cast Off reads boatRegistryState() but never waits for it. Right after a relaunch aboard the state is 'pending', during the 10 s auto-sync deferral and the index fetch, or for longer while the tracer defers the auto-sync. A route checked on her licensed charts is then refused with the 'recheck' sentence.
findings.scenario: Aboard on the boat's Wi-Fi, Shane relaunches and taps Cast Off on a route he checked yesterday within the first ~10-15 s. He is told "Checked on Serene Summer's charts. They open on the boat's Wi-Fi; recheck there before Cast Off." while he is on that Wi-Fi. A retry a few seconds later passes. This misleads and invites a needless recheck.
findings.fix: When boatRegistryState() is 'pending', `await whenBoatRegistrySettled(8_000)` (bounded) before reading getRegistryFingerprint. Keep boatChartsAway only for a state that is still not 'loaded' after the wait.

findings.defect: Registration is O(N²). Each row calls cellMeta.getRegisteredCell, which rebuilds readIdentityGroups over every overlay record and re-parses the open localStorage records. This runs synchronously on the main thread at every registration, including every 10-min auto-sync poll, because registerFromPiIndex runs on every syncEncFromPi.
findings.scenario: With 1,031 held licensed records plus 40 open ones, re-registration costs about 200 ms of lookups on an M-series Mac in jsdom (probe: 196 ms), and likely more on an iPhone WebView. The chart freezes for that long every 10 minutes while she pans.
findings.fix: Build one Map of the held records keyed by storage identity (from listBoatRecords()) before the loop and look rows up in it, instead of calling getRegisteredCell per row.

findings.defect: Eviction runs while a fresh entry still counts its full plain-text length, before its gzip lands. Each multi-MB put therefore evicts several MB of already-compressed cells, about 5-10× more cells than its compressed size needs, and those cells are not restored when the compression shrinks the entry.
findings.scenario: With a full vault after panning, ensureBoatCells or the hydration walk pull three 5-7 MB cells at once through the shared limiter. stored jumps by about 15-21 MB, so evict() drops 15-21 MB of gzip, up to half the vault, which can be hundreds of cells. The compression then lands and the vault sits around 20 MiB. The next merge re-pulls those cells from the Pi, the round trips the 40 MiB sizing was meant to avoid.
findings.fix: Charge a pending entry an estimate (for example text/6) against the budget until its gzip lands, or run evict() only in the compression callback (plus a hard ceiling on plain-text bytes pending).
